theory.title: Peticiones en estilo indirecto y preguntas indirectas
theory.explanation: Para comunicar una petición, usa ask + persona + to + infinitivo: She asked me to explain (me pidió que explicara). En las preguntas indirectas se mantiene el orden de una oración afirmativa (sujeto + verbo): Could you tell me where the museum is? (¿Podría decirme dónde está el museo?).
theory.tip: Mantén el orden sujeto + verbo en preguntas indirectas y usa ask + objeto + to-infinitivo para peticiones.

content.passage: At a cultural centre, visitors asked the guide several questions. One person asked where the exhibition began, while another asked whether photographs were allowed. The guide asked everyone to keep their voices low and not to touch the objects. A visitor politely asked her to explain a traditional ceremony more slowly. The guide was happy to help and suggested that visitors ask questions at the end.

items.prompt: Report a request a visitor might make at a museum.
items.modelAnswer: I believe learning about other cultures helps people become more open-minded. When I visit a new place, I try to respect local customs and learn a few useful expressions. At first, some differences may feel unfamiliar, but people can understand one another if they communicate politely. I enjoy meeting local people because we can share experiences and learn from each other. In the future, I hope to take part in more international exchanges.

content.audioTranscript: A: How was the cultural exchange? B: Great. The students stayed with a local host family. A: Did they learn about local traditions? B: Yes, and they practised the language every day. A: Did they attend the town festival? B: They did. The whole community was involved. A: How did the visitors behave? B: They showed respect and made new friendships.
